title: Live-cell imaging of microglial interactions with radial glia in transgenic embryonic mouse brains using slice culture
protocol: Anaesthetize the pregnant dam using isofluorane and immediately euthanize the animal using cervical dislocation.
Make an incision along the abdomen of the pregnant dam and remove the E15.5 embryos from both uterine horns.
Place the embryos in ice-cold PBS in a Petri dish sitting on ice.
One at a time, place a single embryo into a second Petri dish filled with ice-cold PBS under a dissecting microscope on the benchtop.
Cut off the embryo head and discard the body.
Carefully harvest the E15.5 brain from the head using forceps and a dissecting spoon.
Place the E15.5 brain in a Petri dish filled with ice-cold PBS and place back on ice.
Microwave the 4% LMP agarose until the agarose powder has dissolved and the solution is a clear homogenous liquid.
Place the bottle of 4% LMP agarose on ice with a thermometer in the agarose to measure the temperature.
Place the plastic tissue embedding molds on ice.
Pour the 4% LMP agarose into the plastic molds once the temperature is between 45°C and 55°C.
Place the E15.5 mouse brain into the 4% LMP agarose within the plastic molds when the temperature reaches 40°C.
Use a pipette tip to quickly orient the brain in the 4% LMP agarose before it solidifies.
Transfer the embryonic brain from the PBS to the 4% LMP agarose using a dissecting spoon.
Swirl the agarose around the brain with a pipette tip to dilute any adhered PBS.
Remove or pop any nearby bubbles in the agarose.
Wait for the agarose to solidify.
Tear apart the plastic mold and place the agarose-embedded sample on a Petri dish on ice.
Cut the excess agarose surrounding the embryonic brain using a razor blade.
Adhere the agarose-embedded brain onto the metal vibratome plate with Krazy Glue®.
Attach the metal vibratome plate with the glued sample to the vibratome.
Submerge the sample in the vibratome reservoir containing ice-cold PBS and surround it with ice.
Trim excess agarose surrounding the sample using the vibratome.
Section through brain regions that are not of interest to reach the region of interest.
Collect 300–350 μm vibratome slices using a brush and metal spatula.
Transfer sliced embryonic brain sections from the vibratome sectioning chamber to a cell culture dish.
Place up to three embryonic brain sections on the cell culture insert.
Aspirate excess PBS transferred from the vibratome chamber using a pipette.
Add slice culture medium to the top of each embryonic brain slice.
Achieve AAV viral transduction by applying it with a localized pipette application.
Place the 300–350 μm vibratome slices on the cell culture insert within the glass bottom Petri dishes containing the medium.
Use a pipette to remove any PBS that was transferred from the vibratome sectioning chamber to the cell culture insert.
Add 20–40 μL slice culture medium to the top of each embryonic brain section.
Place the embryonic brain slices atop the culture insert within the glass bottom Petri dish into a cell culture incubator with ambient oxygen and 5% CO2 at 37°C for at least 1–2 h prior to imaging.
Change the slice culture medium daily if the embryonic brain slices remain in the incubator for up to 48 h prior to imaging.
Label radial glia and/or other cells with GFP using AAV2-GFP control virus.
Dilute 1-2 μL of Adeno-associated virus in 5 μL slice culture medium.
Apply the diluted AAV solution to the surface of Cx3cr1CreERT2; Rosa26tdTomato vibratome-sectioned embryonic brain tissue in the region of interest (e.g., hypothalamus).
Incubate the treated tissue in a cell culture incubator with ambient oxygen and 5% CO2 at 37°C for 24-48 hours before imaging.
Aspirate the slice culture medium from glass bottom Petri dishes containing vibratome sectioned embryonic brain slices.
Prepare a solution by mixing 7.5 μL Annexin V conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 with 1,132 μL HBSS and 375 μL 10 mM CaCl2.
Place the prepared solution in the glass bottom Petri dish.
Incubate the Petri dish at room temperature (∼20°C–22°C) for 15 min in the dark.
Wash the glass bottom Petri dish with slice culture medium twice.
Add a final solution of 1.5 mL slice culture medium containing 5.4 μL Annexin V to the Petri dish.
Place the vibratome sectioned embryonic brain slices in a cell culture incubator with ambient oxygen and 5% CO2 at 37°C for 2–48 h before imaging.
Aspirate the slice culture medium from the glass bottom Petri dish.
Apply 1.5 mL of a solution containing 1 μL Hoechst diluted in 7.5 mL of PBS to the glass bottom Petri dish.
Add at least 50 μL of the solution directly onto the brain slice.
Incubate for 10–15 minutes in the dark.
Wash the glass bottom Petri dish with PBS three times.
Add fresh slice culture medium to the glass bottom Petri dish.
Place vibratome sectioned embryonic brain slices in a cell culture incubator at ambient oxygen and 5% CO2, maintaining a temperature of 37°C for 2–48 hours before imaging.
Place glass bottom Petri dishes containing embryonic brain slices atop cell culture inserts in a 37°C heated and humidified imaging chamber.
Expose the Petri dishes to 5% CO2/40% O2 balanced with nitrogen via a gas bubbling system.
Imaging can begin using a Zeiss LSM 700 inverted confocal microscope equipped with a 20× long working distance objective.
Take Z-stacks from the center of the 300–350 μm slice, adjusting pinhole and Z-step size as needed.
Acquire each Z-stack between 5 to 15 minutes, ensuring slices rest for 5 minutes between acquisitions.
Maintain laser power around 2% during imaging.
Set imaging duration according to experimental conditions.
Analyze live-cell imaging videos using ZENBlack software if acquired on a Zeiss microscope.
Use ZENBlack software to convert .czi files to maximum intensity projections for video merging and still image extraction.
Utilize the 3D function in ZENBlack software to generate 3D renderings of microglial-radial glia interactions from original .czi videos.
Image the tissue on an inverted microscope equipped with a long working distance objective.
Ensure the laser power is maintained around 2% to prevent photobleaching and toxicity.
Set the laser power between 6%-8% during imaging due to weak fluorescence from the GlastGFP transgene.
